A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OmniThink. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including equations, tables, prompts, and embedded figures. Relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original WildSeek article and outline evaluations, component ablations, retrieval-depth experiments, and a human study involving 20 topics and 15 evaluators.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds reasoning-model evaluations, retrieval-boundary analyses, an oRAG-Plus comparison, unique-URL counts, and processing-time measurements.

M1.justification: The information-tree/conceptual-pool pipeline, expansion and reflection, outline construction, and article composition remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 moves to Appendix I with identical steps, and all five prompt listings are retained. The slow-thinking terminology and revised explanations do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Coverage remains WildSeek open-domain article and outline generation and the same human-evaluation task. Additional backbone configurations, retrieval controls, and timing analyses remain within this coverage. The AGI examples replace an illustrative AlphaFold article without establishing a new benchmark or distinct task.

E2.justification: v2 Section 5.1 and Figure 6 add oRAG-Plus, which retrieves as many web pages as OmniThink. The original RAG, oRAG, STORM, and Co-STORM comparisons remain. O1-preview and DeepSeek-R1 extend backbone configurations rather than introduce competing writing methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds O1-preview and DeepSeek-R1 configurations, a retrieval-volume-matched control, and a PCA-based retrieval-scope procedure. Appendix D.2 introduces timing over 10 cases using Google Search and Qwen-Plus, separately from the retained Bing-based quality setup. v2 also removes v1's assurance that table results were collected within three days; this does not establish that collection procedures actually changed.

E4.justification: v2 adds retrieval-scope visualization and a control testing whether additional retrieved material alone explains performance, plus unique-URL and processing-time analyses. Appendix G replaces the AlphaFold example with GPT-4o and DeepSeek-R1 AGI cases. The original component ablation, model-substitution analysis, and depth sweep remain as Figure 7(a–c).

E5.justification: Both versions mention multiple evaluation rounds with different prompts and report averages without seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new timing experiment's 10 cases specify sample size. The new 1.5-standard-deviation threshold filters PCA points rather than reporting experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains GPT-4o scores but revises Qwen-Plus results: OmniThink novelty changes from 3.83 to 3.38, and Co-STORM relevance from 4.09 to 3.26, with changed rankings. v2 does not explain these replacements. It adds two reasoning-backbone result blocks and retrieval/control/timing findings, including 120.63 unique URLs for OmniThink and runtime of 322 seconds versus 289 for each reported comparator. Original outline, human, and component/depth results remain.

T1.justification: The KD numerator changes from sum_i k_i U(k_i) in v1 Equation (1) to sum_i U(k_i) in v2 Equation (3), correcting the formal expression to count unique knowledge units. The described fact-decomposition and deduplication procedure remains unchanged. The new boundary terminology is conceptual; no formal proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central claim of improving knowledge density while maintaining article quality, and the model-agnostic conclusion, remain. v2 adds explaining generation constraints through knowledge boundaries to its headline contributions, replacing the validation/expert-feedback contribution. KD becomes an explicit contribution bullet, although v1 already introduced it as a new metric.

C2.justification: v2 develops a distinct information-boundary/cognition-boundary explanation and interprets oRAG-Plus degradation as inadequate information utilization and noise. For the retained depth curve, v1 suggests approaching the topic's search limit, whereas v2 argues that other unidentified boundaries become limiting. New case-study and runtime interpretations accompany this shift. The stated limitations and human-versus-automatic evaluation caveats are retained.

D1.justification: v2 documents snippet embeddings, PCA, normalization, outlier filtering, and convex-hull construction in Appendix E, and names qwen-plus-2024-08-06 for the retained component analysis in Appendix F. It also supplies timing setup details. Core generation settings, prompt texts, retrieval counts, and code/demo access links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations supporting cognition and agentic-reasoning framing, including Chemero, Riva, and Wu, alongside Lewis and Xia. References to Qiao's prompting survey, Qin's o1 report, Collaborative Gym, and Quiet-STaR disappear. Related-work positioning shifts toward updating cognitive frameworks, while STORM and Co-STORM remain central reference points.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized and rewritten around knowledge boundaries. KD moves from Background to Experiments, human evaluation and pseudocode move into appendices, and previously separate ablation and depth sections are consolidated. The introduction, contribution list, method explanations, analysis, and related-work discussion receive substantial revisions.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 5–6 and Tables 3–4, expands Table 1 with grouped conversational/reasoning-model blocks, and redraws and combines v1 Figures 5–7 into Figure 7. Human-evaluation displays move to the appendix, the AlphaFold case is replaced by two AGI displays, and prompt/rubric layouts are redistributed.

improvement.justification: The retrieval-volume control, additional backbone evaluations, and URL/timing analyses improve empirical scrutiny, while the KD formula correction improves precision and the human study is preserved. These gains are limited by unexplained Qwen-Plus score replacements, removal of the three-day collection assurance, and boundary interpretations that go beyond what the PCA visualization and depth plateau establish.
